NKJV.1: Then Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood; two and a half cubits was its length, a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
NKJV.2: He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold all around it.
NKJV.3: And he cast for it four rings of gold to be set in its four corners: two rings on one side, and two rings on the other side of it.
NKJV.4: He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
NKJV.5: And he put the poles into the rings at the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
NKJV.6: He also made the mercy seat of pure gold; two and a half cubits was its length and a cubit and a half its width.
NKJV.7: He made two cherubim of beaten gold; he made them of one piece at the two ends of the mercy seat:
NKJV.8: one cherub at one end on this side, and the other cherub at the other end on that side. He made the cherubim at the two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.
NKJV.9: The cherubim spread out their wings above, and covered the mercy seat with their wings. They faced one another; the faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
NKJV.10: He made the table of acacia wood; two cubits was its length, a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
NKJV.11: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made a molding of gold all around it.
NKJV.12: Also he made a frame of a handbreadth all around it, and made a molding of gold for the frame all around it.
NKJV.13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that were at its four legs.
NKJV.14: The rings were close to the frame, as holders for the poles to bear the table.
NKJV.15: And he made the poles of acacia wood to bear the table, and overlaid them with gold.
NKJV.16: He made of pure gold the utensils which were on the table: its dishes, its cups, its bowls, and its pitchers for pouring.
NKJV.17: He also made the lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work he made the lampstand. Its shaft, its branches, its bowls, its ornamental knobs, and its flowers were of the same piece.
NKJV.18: And six branches came out of its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side.
NKJV.19: There were three bowls made like almond blossoms on one branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower, and three bowls made like almond blossoms on the other branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower—and so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.
NKJV.20: And on the lampstand itself were four bowls made like almond blossoms, each with its ornamental knob and flower.
NKJV.21: There was a knob under the first two branches of the same, a knob under the second two branches of the same, and a knob under the third two branches of the same, according to the six branches extending from it.
NKJV.22: Their knobs and their branches were of one piece; all of it was one hammered piece of pure gold.
NKJV.23: And he made its seven lamps, its wick-trimmers, and its trays of pure gold.
NKJV.24: Of a talent of pure gold he made it, with all its utensils.
NKJV.25: He made the incense altar of acacia wood. Its length was a cubit and its width a cubit—it was square—and two cubits was its height. Its horns were of one piece with it.
NKJV.26: And he overlaid it with pure gold: its top, its sides all around, and its horns. He also made for it a molding of gold all around it.
NKJV.27: He made two rings of gold for it under its molding, by its two corners on both sides, as holders for the poles with which to bear it.
NKJV.28: And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
NKJV.29: He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the perfumer.

ESV.1: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Two cubits  and a half was its length, a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
ESV.2: And he overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold around it.
ESV.3: And he cast for it four rings of gold for its four feet, two rings on its one side and two rings on its other side.
ESV.4: And he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold
ESV.5: and put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
ESV.6: And he made a mercy seat of pure gold. Two cubits and a half was its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth.
ESV.7: And he made two cherubim of gold. He made them of hammered work on the two ends of the mercy seat,
ESV.8: one cherub on the one end, and one cherub on the other end. Of one piece with the mercy seat he made the cherubim on its two ends.
ESV.9: The cherubim spread out their wings above, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces one to another; toward the mercy seat were the faces of the cherubim.
ESV.10: He also made the table of acacia wood. Two cubits was its length, a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
ESV.11: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made a molding of gold around it.
ESV.12: And he made a rim around it a handbreadth  wide, and made a molding of gold around the rim.
ESV.13: He cast for it four rings of gold and fastened the rings to the four corners at its four legs.
ESV.14: Close to the frame were the rings, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
ESV.15: He made the poles of acacia wood to carry the table, and overlaid them with gold.
ESV.16: And he made the vessels of pure gold that were to be on the table, its plates and dishes for incense, and its bowls and flagons with which to pour drink offerings.
ESV.17: He also made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work. Its base, its stem, its cups, its calyxes, and its flowers were of one piece with it.
ESV.18: And there were six branches going out of its sides, three branches of the lampstand out of one side of it and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side of it;
ESV.19: three cups made like almond blossoms, each with calyx and flower, on one branch, and three cups made like almond blossoms, each with calyx and flower, on the other branch — so for the six branches going out of the lampstand.
ESV.20: And on the lampstand itself were four cups made like almond blossoms, with their calyxes and flowers,
ESV.21: and a calyx of one piece with it under each pair of the six branches going out of it.
ESV.22: Their calyxes and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole of it was a single piece of hammered work of pure gold.
ESV.23: And he made its seven lamps and its tongs and its trays of pure gold.
ESV.24: He made it and all its utensils out of a talent  of pure gold.
ESV.25: He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. Its length was a cubit, and its breadth was a cubit. It was square, and two cubits was its height. Its horns were of one piece with it.
ESV.26: He overlaid it with pure gold, its top and around its sides and its horns. And he made a molding of gold around it,
ESV.27: and made two rings of gold on it under its molding, on two opposite sides of it, as holders for the poles with which to carry it.
ESV.28: And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
ESV.29: He made the holy anointing oil also, and the pure fragrant incense, blended as by the perfumer.

NASB.1: Now Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood; its length was two and a half cubits, and its width one and a half cubits, and its height one and a half cubits;
NASB.2: and he overlaid it with pure gold inside and out, and made a gold molding for it all around.
NASB.3: He cast four rings of gold for it on its four feet; even two rings on one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.
NASB.4: He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NASB.5: He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
NASB.6: He made a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
NASB.7: He made two cherubim of gold; he made them of hammered work at the two ends of the mercy seat;
NASB.8: one cherub at the one end and one cherub at the other end; he made the cherubim [of one piece] with the mercy seat at the two ends.
NASB.9: The cherubim had [their] wings spread upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward each other; the faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
NASB.10: Then he made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long and a cubit wide and one and a half cubits high.
NASB.11: He overlaid it with pure gold, and made a gold molding for it all around.
NASB.12: He made a rim for it of a handbreadth all around, and made a gold molding for its rim all around.
NASB.13: He cast four gold rings for it and put the rings on the four corners that were on its four feet.
NASB.14: Close by the rim were the rings, the holders for the poles to carry the table.
NASB.15: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.
NASB.16: He made the utensils which were on the table, its dishes and its pans and its bowls and its jars, with which to pour out drink offerings, of pure gold.
NASB.17: Then he made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work, its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its flowers were [of one piece] with it.
NASB.18: There were six branches going out of its sides; three branches of the lampstand from the one side of it and three branches of the lampstand from the other side of it;
NASB.19: three cups shaped like almond [blossoms], a bulb and a flower in one branch, and three cups shaped like almond [blossoms], a bulb and a flower in the other branch-- so for the six branches going out of the lampstand.
NASB.20: In the lampstand [there were] four cups shaped like almond [blossoms], its bulbs and its flowers;
NASB.21: and a bulb was under the [first] pair of branches [coming] out of it, and a bulb under the [second] pair of branches [coming] out of it, and a bulb under the [third] pair of branches [coming] out of it, for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.
NASB.22: Their bulbs and their branches were [of one piece] with it; the whole of it [was] a single hammered work of pure gold.
NASB.23: He made its seven lamps with its snuffers and its trays of pure gold.
NASB.24: He made it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
NASB.25: Then he made the altar of incense of acacia wood: a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, and two cubits high; its horns were [of one piece] with it.
NASB.26: He overlaid it with pure gold, its top and its sides all around, and its horns; and he made a gold molding for it all around.
NASB.27: He made two golden rings for it under its molding, on its two sides-- on opposite sides-- as holders for poles with which to carry it.
NASB.28: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NASB.29: And he made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense of spices, the work of a perfumer.

NLT.1: Next Bezalel made the Ark of acacia wood — a sacred chest 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high.
NLT.2: He overlaid it inside and outside with pure gold, and he ran a molding of gold all around it.
NLT.3: He cast four gold rings and attached them to its four feet, two rings on each side.
NLT.4: Then he made poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NLT.5: He inserted the poles into the rings at the sides of the Ark to carry it.
NLT.6: Then he made the Ark’s cover — the place of atonement — from pure gold. It was 45 inches long and 27 inches wide.
NLT.7: He made two cherubim from hammered gold and placed them on the two ends of the atonement cover.
NLT.8: He molded the cherubim on each end of the atonement cover, making it all of one piece of gold.
NLT.9: The cherubim faced each other and looked down on the atonement cover. With their wings spread above it, they protected it.
NLT.10: Then Bezalel made the table of acacia wood, 36 inches long, 18 inches wide, and 27 inches high.
NLT.11: He overlaid it with pure gold and ran a gold molding around the edge.
NLT.12: He decorated it with a 3-inch border all around, and he ran a gold molding along the border.
NLT.13: Then he cast four gold rings for the table and attached them at the four corners next to the four legs.
NLT.14: The rings were attached near the border to hold the poles that were used to carry the table.
NLT.15: He made these poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NLT.16: Then he made special containers of pure gold for the table — bowls, ladles, jars, and pitchers — to be used in pouring out liquid offerings.
NLT.17: Then Bezalel made the lampstand of pure, hammered gold. He made the entire lampstand and its decorations of one piece — the base, center stem, lamp cups, buds, and petals.
NLT.18: The lampstand had six branches going out from the center stem, three on each side.
NLT.19: Each of the six branches had three lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
NLT.20: The center stem of the lampstand was crafted with four lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
NLT.21: There was an almond bud beneath each pair of branches where the six branches extended from the center stem, all made of one piece.
NLT.22: The almond buds and branches were all of one piece with the center stem, and they were hammered from pure gold.
NLT.23: He also made seven lamps for the lampstand, lamp snuffers, and trays, all of pure gold.
NLT.24: The entire lampstand, along with its accessories, was made from 75 pounds of pure gold.
NLT.25: Then Bezalel made the incense altar of acacia wood. It was 18 inches square and 36 inches high, with horns at the corners carved from the same piece of wood as the altar itself.
NLT.26: He overlaid the top, sides, and horns of the altar with pure gold, and he ran a gold molding around the entire altar.
NLT.27: He made two gold rings and attached them on opposite sides of the altar below the gold molding to hold the carrying poles.
NLT.28: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NLT.29: Then he made the sacred anointing oil and the fragrant incense, using the techniques of a skilled incense maker.

CSB17.1: Bezalel <sup>ⓛ</sup> made the ark of acacia wood, forty-five inches long, twenty-seven inches wide, and twenty-seven inches high. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.2: He overlaid it with pure gold inside and out and made a gold molding all around it.
CSB17.3: He cast four gold rings for it, for its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
CSB17.4: He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
CSB17.5: He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark for carrying the ark.
CSB17.6: He made a mercy seat of pure gold, forty-five inches long and twenty-seven inches wide. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.7: He made two cherubim of gold; he made them of hammered work at the two ends of the mercy seat,
CSB17.8: one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. At each end, he made a cherub of one piece with the mercy seat.
CSB17.9: They had wings spread out. They faced each other and covered the mercy seat with their wings. The faces of the cherubim were looking toward the mercy seat.
CSB17.10: He <sup>ⓜ</sup> constructed the table of acacia wood, thirty-six inches long, eighteen inches wide, and twenty-seven inches high. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.11: He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding all around it.
CSB17.12: He made a three-inch <sup>[4]</sup> frame all around it and made a gold molding all around its frame.
CSB17.13: He cast four gold rings for it and attached the rings to the four corners at its four legs.
CSB17.14: The rings were next to the frame as holders for the poles to carry the table.
CSB17.15: He made the poles for carrying the table from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
CSB17.16: He also made the utensils that would be on the table out of pure gold: its plates and cups, as well as its bowls and pitchers for pouring drink offerings.
CSB17.17: Then <sup>ⓝ</sup> he made the lampstand out of pure hammered gold. He made it all of one piece: its base and shaft, its ornamental cups, and its buds and petals.
CSB17.18: Six branches extended from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.
CSB17.19: There were three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and petals, on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and petals, on the next branch. It was this way for the six branches that extended from the lampstand.
CSB17.20: There were four cups shaped like almond blossoms on the lampstand shaft along with its buds and petals.
CSB17.21: For the six branches that extended from it, a bud was under the first pair of branches from it, a bud under the second pair of branches from it, and a bud under the third pair of branches from it.
CSB17.22: Their buds and branches were of one piece with it. All of it was a single hammered piece of pure gold.
CSB17.23: He also made its seven lamps, snuffers, and firepans of pure gold.
CSB17.24: He made it and all its utensils of seventy-five pounds <sup>[5]</sup> of pure gold.
CSB17.25: He <sup>ⓐ</sup> made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, eighteen inches long and eighteen inches wide; it was thirty-six inches high. <sup>[6]</sup> Its horns were of one piece with it.
CSB17.26: He overlaid it, its top, all around its sides, and its horns with pure gold. Then he made a gold molding all around it.
CSB17.27: He made two gold rings for it under the molding on two of its sides; he put these on opposite sides of it to be holders for the poles to carry it with.
CSB17.28: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
CSB17.29: He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant, and expertly blended incense. <sup>ⓑ</sup>

WEB.1: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits,  and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
WEB.2: He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold for it around it.
WEB.3: He cast four rings of gold for it, in its four feet; even two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side.
WEB.4: He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
WEB.5: He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
WEB.6: He made a mercy seat of pure gold. Its length was two and a half cubits, and a cubit and a half its width.
WEB.7: He made two cherubim of gold. He made them of beaten work, at the two ends of the mercy seat;
WEB.8: one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat at its two ends.
WEB.9: The cherubim spread out their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward one another. The faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
WEB.10: He made the table of acacia wood. Its length was two cubits, and its width was a cubit, and its height was a cubit and a half.
WEB.11: He overlaid it with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
WEB.12: He made a border of a hand width around it, and made a golden molding on its border around it.
WEB.13: He cast four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that were on its four feet.
WEB.14: The rings were close by the border, the places for the poles to carry the table.
WEB.15: He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.
WEB.16: He made the vessels which were on the table, its dishes, its spoons, its bowls, and its pitchers with which to pour out, of pure gold.
WEB.17: He made the lamp stand of pure gold. He made the lamp stand of beaten work. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers were of one piece with it.
WEB.18: There were six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side:
WEB.19: three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower, and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower: so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
WEB.20: In the lamp stand were four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;
WEB.21: and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of it.
WEB.22: Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole thing was one beaten work of pure gold.
WEB.23: He made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of pure gold.
WEB.24: He made it of a talent  of pure gold, with all its vessels.
WEB.25: He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. It was square: its length was a cubit, and its width a cubit. Its height was two cubits. Its horns were of one piece with it.
WEB.26: He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, its sides around it, and its horns. He made a gold molding around it.
WEB.27: He made two golden rings for it under its molding crown, on its two ribs, on its two sides, for places for poles with which to carry it.
WEB.28: He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
WEB.29: He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, after the art of the perfumer.

AMP.1: Bezalel made the ark [of the covenant] of acacia wood—it was two and a half cubits long, and one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
AMP.2: And he overlaid it with pure gold inside and out, and made a molding (border) of gold to go all around [the top of it].
AMP.3: He cast four rings of gold for it on its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
AMP.4: He made carrying poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
AMP.5: He put the carrying poles through the rings at the sides of the ark, to carry it.
AMP.6: Bezalel made the mercy seat of pure gold; it was two and a half cubits long, and one and a half cubits wide.
AMP.7: He made two cherubim of hammered gold; he made them at the two ends of the mercy seat,
AMP.8: one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end; he made the cherubim [of one piece] with the mercy seat at the two ends.
AMP.9: The cherubim spread out their wings upward, covering and protecting the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward each other; the faces of the cherubim were [looking downward] toward the mercy seat.
AMP.10: Bezalel made the table [for the bread] of acacia wood; it was two cubits long, a cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
AMP.11: He overlaid it with pure gold, and made a border of gold for it all around [its top].
AMP.12: He made a rim for it [just under the top] a hand width wide all around, and a border of gold around its rim.
AMP.13: He cast four rings of gold for it and fastened the rings to the four corners that were at its four legs.
AMP.14: Close by the rim were the rings, the holders for the poles [to pass through] to carry the table.
AMP.15: Bezalel made the carrying poles of acacia wood to carry the table and overlaid them with gold.
AMP.16: He made the utensils which were to be on the table, its dishes and its pans [for bread], its bowls and its jars for pouring drink offerings, of pure gold.
AMP.17: Then he made the lampstand (menorah) of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work, its base and its [center] shaft; its cups, its calyxes, and its flowers were all of one piece with it.
AMP.18: There were six branches coming out of the sides of the lampstand, three branches from one side of the center shaft and three branches from the other side of it;
AMP.19: three cups shaped like almond blossoms, a calyx and a flower in one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, a calyx and a flower in the opposite branch—so for the six branches coming out of the center shaft of the lampstand.
AMP.20: On the center shaft of the lampstand there were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with calyxes and flowers [one at the top];
AMP.21: and a calyx was under the first pair of branches coming out of it, and a calyx under the second pair of branches, coming out of it, and a calyx under the third pair of branches coming out of it, for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.
AMP.22: Their calyxes and their branches were of one piece with it; all of it was a single hammered work of pure gold.
AMP.23: He made its seven lamps with its snuffers and its trays of pure gold.
AMP.24: He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
AMP.25: Then Bezalel made the incense altar of acacia wood; its top was a cubit square and it was two cubits high; the horns were of one piece with it.
AMP.26: He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, its sides all around and its horns; he also made a rim of gold around it.
AMP.27: He made two rings of gold for it under its rim, on its two opposite sides, as holders for the poles [to pass through] to carry it.
AMP.28: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
AMP.29: He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense of spices, the work of a perfumer.

MSG.1: Bezalel made the Chest using acacia wood: He made it three and three-quarters feet long and two and a quarter feet wide and deep.
MSG.2: He covered it inside and out with a veneer of pure gold and made a molding of gold all around it.
MSG.3: He cast four gold rings and attached them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
MSG.4: He made poles from acacia wood, covered them with a veneer of gold,
MSG.5: and inserted the poles for carrying the Chest into the rings on the sides.
MSG.6: Next he made a lid of pure gold for the Chest, an Atonement-Cover, three and three-quarters feet long and two and a quarter feet wide.
MSG.7: He sculpted two winged angel-cherubim out of hammered gold for the ends of the Atonement-Cover,
MSG.8: one angel at one end, one angel at the other. He made them of one piece with the Atonement-Cover.
MSG.9: The angels had outstretched wings and appeared to hover over the Atonement-Cover, facing one another but looking down on the Atonement-Cover.
MSG.10: He made the Table from acacia wood. He made it three feet long, one and a half feet wide and two and a quarter feet high.
MSG.11: He covered it with a veneer of pure gold and made a molding of gold all around it.
MSG.12: He made a border a handbreadth wide all around it and a rim of gold for the border.
MSG.13: He cast four rings of gold for it and attached the rings to the four legs
MSG.14: parallel to the table top. They will serve as holders for the poles used to carry the Table.
MSG.15: He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with a veneer of gold. They will be used to carry the Table.
MSG.16: Out of pure gold he made the utensils for the Table: its plates, bowls, jars, and jugs used for pouring.
MSG.17: He made a Lampstand of pure hammered gold, making its stem and branches, cups, calyxes, and petals all of one piece.
MSG.18: It had six branches, three from one side and three from the other;
MSG.19: three cups shaped like almond blossoms with calyxes and petals on one branch, three on the next, and so on—the same for all six branches.
MSG.20: On the main stem of the Lampstand, there were four cups shaped like almonds, with calyxes and petals,
MSG.21: a calyx extending from under each pair of the six branches.
MSG.22: The entire Lampstand with its calyxes and stems was fashioned from one piece of hammered pure gold.
MSG.23: He made seven of these lamps with their candle snuffers, all out of pure gold.
MSG.24: He used a seventy-five-pound brick of pure gold to make the Lampstand and its accessories.
MSG.25: He made an Altar for burning incense from acacia wood. He made it a foot and a half square and three feet high, with its horns of one piece with it.
MSG.26: He covered it with a veneer of pure gold, its top, sides, and horns, and made a gold molding around it
MSG.27: with two rings of gold beneath the molding. He placed the rings on the two opposing sides to serve as holders for poles by which it will be carried.
MSG.28: He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with a veneer of gold.
MSG.29: He also prepared with the art of a perfumer the holy anointing oil and the pure aromatic incense.

NRSVCE.1: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood; it was two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
NRSVCE.2: He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold around it.
NRSVCE.3: He cast for it four rings of gold for its four feet, two rings on its one side and two rings on its other side.
NRSVCE.4: He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold,
NRSVCE.5: and put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.
NRSVCE.6: He made a mercy seat of pure gold; two cubits and a half was its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
NRSVCE.7: He made two cherubim of hammered gold; at the two ends of the mercy seat he made them,
NRSVCE.8: one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end; of one piece with the mercy seat he made the cherubim at its two ends.
NRSVCE.9: The cherubim spread out their wings above, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings. They faced one another; the faces of the cherubim were turned toward the mercy seat.
NRSVCE.10: He also made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
NRSVCE.11: He overlaid it with pure gold, and made a molding of gold around it.
NRSVCE.12: He made around it a rim a handbreadth wide, and made a molding of gold around the rim.
NRSVCE.13: He cast for it four rings of gold, and fastened the rings to the four corners at its four legs.
NRSVCE.14: The rings that held the poles used for carrying the table were close to the rim.
NRSVCE.15: He made the poles of acacia wood to carry the table, and overlaid them with gold.
NRSVCE.16: And he made the vessels of pure gold that were to be on the table, its plates and dishes for incense, and its bowls and flagons with which to pour drink offerings.
NRSVCE.17: He also made the lampstand of pure gold. The base and the shaft of the lampstand were made of hammered work; its cups, its calyxes, and its petals were of one piece with it.
NRSVCE.18: There were six branches going out of its sides, three branches of the lampstand out of one side of it and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side of it;
NRSVCE.19: three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with calyx and petals, on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with calyx and petals, on the other branch — so for the six branches going out of the lampstand.
NRSVCE.20: On the lampstand itself there were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with its calyxes and petals.
NRSVCE.21: There was a calyx of one piece with it under the first pair of branches, a calyx of one piece with it under the next pair of branches, and a calyx of one piece with it under the last pair of branches.
NRSVCE.22: Their calyxes and their branches were of one piece with it, the whole of it one hammered piece of pure gold.
NRSVCE.23: He made its seven lamps and its snuffers and its trays of pure gold.
NRSVCE.24: He made it and all its utensils of a talent of pure gold.
NRSVCE.25: He made the altar of incense of acacia wood, one cubit long, and one cubit wide; it was square, and was two cubits high; its horns were of one piece with it.
NRSVCE.26: He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, and its sides all around, and its horns; and he made for it a molding of gold all around,
NRSVCE.27: and made two golden rings for it under its molding, on two opposite sides of it, to hold the poles with which to carry it.
NRSVCE.28: And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
NRSVCE.29: He made the holy anointing oil also, and the pure fragrant incense, blended as by the perfumer.

NIV.1:
The Ark
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood—two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
NIV.2: He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.
NIV.3: He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
NIV.4: Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NIV.5: And he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it.
NIV.6: He made the atonement cover of pure gold—two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
NIV.7: Then he made two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover.
NIV.8: He made one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other; at the two ends he made them of one piece with the cover.
NIV.9: The cherubim had their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the cover.
NIV.10:
The Table
They made the table of acacia wood—two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
NIV.11: Then they overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
NIV.12: They also made around it a rim a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
NIV.13: They cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners, where the four legs were.
NIV.14: The rings were put close to the rim to hold the poles used in carrying the table.
NIV.15: The poles for carrying the table were made of acacia wood and were overlaid with gold.
NIV.16: And they made from pure gold the articles for the table—its plates and dishes and bowls and its pitchers for the pouring out of drink offerings.
NIV.17:
The Lampstand
They made the lampstand of pure gold and hammered it out, base and shaft; its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms were of one piece with it.
NIV.18: Six branches extended from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.
NIV.19: Three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms were on one branch, three on the next branch and the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
NIV.20: And on the lampstand were four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms.
NIV.21: One bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair—six branches in all.
NIV.22: The buds and the branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
NIV.23: They made its seven lamps, as well as its wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold.
NIV.24: They made the lampstand and all its accessories from one talent of pure gold.
NIV.25:
The Altar of Incense
They made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high—its horns of one piece with it.
NIV.26: They overlaid the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
NIV.27: They made two gold rings below the molding—two on opposite sides—to hold the poles used to carry it.
NIV.28: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
NIV.29: They also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense—the work of a perfumer.

NET.1: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood; its length was three feet nine inches, its width two feet three inches, and its height two feet three inches.

NET.3: He cast four gold rings for it that he put on its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
NET.4: He made poles of acacia wood, overlaid them with gold,
NET.5: and put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark in order to carry the ark.

NET.7: He made two cherubim of gold; he made them of hammered metal on the two ends of the atonement lid,
NET.8: one cherub on one end and one cherub on the other end. He made the cherubim from the atonement lid on its two ends.
NET.9: The cherubim were spreading their wings upward, overshadowing the atonement lid with their wings. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the atonement lid.
NET.10: He made the table of acacia wood; its length was three feet, its width one foot six inches, and its height two feet three inches.
NET.11: He overlaid it with pure gold, and he made a surrounding border of gold for it.
NET.12: He made a surrounding frame for it about three inches wide, and he made a surrounding border of gold for its frame.

NET.14: The rings were close to the frame to provide places for the poles to carry the table.
NET.15: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.

NET.20: On the lampstand there were four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms,
NET.21: with a bud under the first two branches from it, and a bud under the next two branches from it, and a bud under the third two branches from it; according to the six branches that extended from it.
